sol.problem:
An unrelated non-permutation gate erases known-clean surrounding workspace from borrow analysis. Exact memoryless ptr_width=32 signature: {"abi":"0.8","args":[],"bounds":[],"in":[],"kind":"action","mem":[],"mut":[1],"tier":"q"}. Function:
action @a (t:wire mut) () () () ()
^entry():
c = qalloc any 1
h t
b = qborrow any 1
cx c b
qreturn b
h t
qfree c
The independently computed interface/closure hash is ba813954a842962eecd96263d6dbe2f549f7f8d4c99241c660f0a3c7626cf10a; with that stored hash object_hash is db747f53ae732bd2cef0eeeaed48b8bb2a523dc74f53b38d2876601a3760445f. hash, check, run-action a --mut 1 and reverse a --mut 1 all exit 1 with empty stdout and §5.6: qreturn does not restore borrowed wire v2_0. Hand: c is always |0>, hence CX(c,b) is identity at this lifetime for every unknown/entangled b; H(t);H(t)=I and c is freed clean. Removing both H instructions accepts and runs/reverses as identity. An independent in-memory harness bypassing only parse admission executes the H-separated body as exact identity in each direction on all four t,b basis pairs, superposition, and b entangled with an untouched reference. decide_frames partitions at Other(H t), then factorises initializes c as a free variable because its Alloc lies in the preceding run. No certificate or budget is involved.
sol.fix: Change src/borrow.rs::Object::decide_frames/factorises and their analysis-state plumbing. §4.3 says qalloc produces "n clean wires"; §5.2 domain D specifies "qalloc'ed wires at 0"; §14.2 says "qalloc tensors |0⟩"; §5.6 requires the frame to satisfy "P_F = P′ ⊗ I_B". Carry established facts about still-live, untouched workspace across a non-permutation boundary, invalidating facts affected by that operation while keeping fresh borrowed entries independent and preserving the mandatory permutation-only borrowed-touch check. H on t must not make c arbitrary. Add the exact fixture to tests/r1_borrow.rs and tests/cli_xam.rs: parse/hash/check must accept; forward and adjoint at t=0/1 and a superposition must preserve t; reverse must report equals_entry=true; library execution must preserve b entangled with an external reference. Also put H after qborrow and before CX, and wrap the lifetime in a loop. Negative control: X c before borrowing and X c after return for explicit cleanup must still reject each one-CX lifetime, including with a correctly bound certificate. This is a reachable-state proof requirement, not permission to merge frames across H or waive a return.

sol.section: §§3.3, 4.3, 4.6, 5.3 adjoint table; src/action.rs::infer_widths, Environment::widths and Object::action_sequence
sol.fix: Change src/action.rs::infer_widths, Environment::widths and action_sequence so lifetime resolution respects structured execution and the actual producer matched to each dynamic release. §4.6 defines qloop as "body n times"; §4.3 defines qalloc as "n clean wires"; §3.3 makes a consumed name unavailable until a new production; §5.3 defines the adjoint in "reverse order, instruction replaced, versions renumbered". A zero-trip body must have no effect on the outer live-width environment. A source-line id alone cannot identify both releases of differently sized lifetimes at different loop iterations; derive the loop entry/iteration-specific matching widths (or an equivalent sound structured lifetime representation) for reverse traversal, without adding a trip-count restriction or banning these well-formed objects. Add both exact fixtures to tests/quantum.rs and tests/cli_xam.rs. For t=0/1 and superposed t, check, forward, adjoint independently, and reverse must all succeed, preserve the complete input and leave no workspace; reverse must report equals_entry=true. Cover nested zero-trip loops, the analogous qborrow/qreturn case, and alpha-renamed unrollings of the changing-width loop. Retain the original R5 straight-line reused-width fixture and live-name redefinition rejection.

codex.fix: Change src/action.rs::infer_widths to model qloop's executed lifetime environment. At n=0, do not propagate any body producer/consumer changes into the outer live map (skip runtime width inference for the dead body, or analyze it with an isolated clone); keep lexical qregion hoisting and normal static validation intact. §4.6 defines qloop as 'body n times'; §4.3 defines qalloc as 'n clean wires' and qfree as release of a bundle 'clean on every basis configuration'; §5.3 requires the adjoint in 'reverse order' with 'versions renumbered'. Therefore this exact object must execute identity for t=0/1 and arbitrary superpositions in either direction, and reverse must report equals_entry=true with no remaining workspace. Add it to tests/quantum.rs and tests/cli_xam.rs, checking the pinned hashes, check success, forward/adjoint state equality and reversal. Add nested zero-trip variants and dead qcopy/quncopy and qborrow/qreturn lifetime changes. Retain SOL-R5-B03's width-1 then width-2 reused-name positive and rejection of producing a still-live name. No execution budget or certificate is involved.

codex.problem:
The clean-entry repair is confined to one permutation run: an unrelated non-permutation gate discards an established clean allocation and causes rejection of a valid action. Exact memoryless ptr_width=32 signature: {"abi":"0.8","args":[],"bounds":[],"in":[],"kind":"action","mem":[],"mut":[1],"tier":"q"}. Function:
action @a (t:wire mut) () () () ()
^entry():
c = qalloc any 1
h t
b = qborrow any 1
qreturn b
qfree c
Independently computed interface/closure H=6c7101e365eccc827653aa5dc596d68fefae112b9e4b6df00b5078f5639bf7d3; stored-H object_hash=e5517c39c82f32f9c006828c6b9535d899dad9c0a7b59339ba9fabea3672fc3f. hash/check/run-action/reverse all exit 1 with empty stdout and '§5.6: a wire released inside a borrow frame is not clean'. Hand: c stays |0>, b is untouched for its entire lifetime, and the operation is H on t tensor identity on b and every external reference. There is no gate on c or b and no window dependency on t. Moving only h t after qfree c gives H=ec71f6ec8d4ff0efca8dd1faff95c483aed5ece49e92e00ec64ef1602ff78818; check succeeds, forward t=1 gives amplitudes +1/sqrt(2), -1/sqrt(2), adjoint t=0 gives two +1/sqrt(2) amplitudes, and reverse restores t=1. Adding x b; x b before qreturn also wrongly rejects the separated positive, so the issue is not peculiar to an empty borrowed circuit. decide_frames starts a fresh factorises evaluation after Other(H t), initializes c as an arbitrary variable, and tests the trailing Free against zero without its earlier allocation. This is a newly exposed boundary case, not a failure of the exact round-5 loop witnesses.
codex.fix: Change src/borrow.rs::decide_frames/factorises so cleanup obligations use established lifetime/cleanliness facts across frame boundaries on disjoint wires. Separate the full-domain borrow-factorisation check from unrelated workspace release obligations, or carry sound entry constraints into each run; do not universally quantify a known-zero c merely because H touched t. §4.3 says qalloc produces 'n clean wires'; §14.2 says 'qalloc tensors |0⟩' and 'qfree removes clean factors'; §6.1 gives qalloc 'perm, S = ∅'; §6.2 closes windows on wires in the dependency set or the value itself. §5.6 still requires 'P_F = P′ ⊗ I_B' for every actual frame. Add the exact positive and the doubled-X-on-b variant to tests/r1_borrow.rs, including hash/check and CLI forward/adjoint t=0/1: expected H|0>=(|0>+|1>)/sqrt(2), H|1>=(|0>-|1>)/sqrt(2), reverse equals_entry=true. In library tests use b entangled with an untouched reference and require H_t tensor I_bR with no workspace. Retain the dirty control x c before release (reject §6.2), one-X-on-b control (reject §5.6), and every round-4/5 invalid-return/certificate negative. No certificate or budget should be required for this positive.
